relevance_note: Case series and scoping review describing individual GAMT deficiency patients, e.g. 'a 6-year-old male with a homozygous pathogenic variant in the GAMT gene'.
method_note: Read the whole paper. A Python script in the scratch directory transcribed Table 1 (own cases, labels 'Case 1'-'Case 4', rule 1) and Table 2 (45 literature cases with no label column; labelled 'Table 2 row k', k = 1..45 counting data rows; the Authors cell is copied to source_reference_in_review); I checked the transcription against both tables. Table spans run from the row start through the cell, extended rightwards where the shorter prefix is not unique. Both table titles define '+/−' as presence/absence; cells with '−' (U+2212) are recorded as excluded with that legend as second span. Two Table 2 cells use an ASCII hyphen '-' (row 34 Behavioral abnormalities; row 42 Hypotonia) instead of the defined symbol and were left not reported; row 31 (Viau, 1 years) has empty phenotype cells (not reported). 'Atypical symptoms' column not turned into feature rows (an undefined category). Checklist mapping: Seizures->seizures or epilepsy; Developmental delay or Intellectual disability '+'->developmental delay or intellectual disability (excluded only when both columns are '−'); Autism '+'->autistic features ('−' autism diagnosis does not exclude the broader item); Hypotonia->hypotonia. 'Movement and tone disorders' and 'Behavioral abnormalities' are composite categories and were not used to exclude any specific checklist item. Normal brain MRI (Cases 1, 2) and 'no structural etiology' (Case 3) recorded as a whole-MRI feature only; no MRI checklist item excluded. Case 1 'normal power, tone, and reflexes' excludes hypotonia and spasticity (hypertonia). ADHD (Cases 2, 4) recorded as hyperactivity observed; Case 2 'restricted language development' as absent or limited speech observed. Discussion details were attached to Table 2 rows only when the match was unambiguous (single row for the reference, or age/sex match): rows 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 13, 20, 34. Not attached (ambiguous): Caldeira female 'presented at 5 months ... diagnosed at the age of 19 years' (could be row 12 or row 14); Hinnell 'Turkish female' described at 25 and 31 years in text but two rows (17 and 18) in Table 2; Leuzzi [38] cerebellar findings (rows 36 and 41). Table 2 variant rows: only zygosity is printed (Genetic mutation column), no variant description or gene symbol in the row, so variant_original_string and gene_symbol are 'not reported'; 'Hemizygote'/'Hemizygous' recorded as hemizygous as printed although the paper calls the disease autosomal recessive; no rows for 'NA'. Contradictions: Stern (row 7) Autism '−' in Table 2 vs 'autism' in text (both rows emitted; checklist autistic features not reported); O'Rourke (row 20) Intellectual disability '−' vs 'Her intellectual disability' in text (both rows; checklist item stays observed via developmental delay '+'); Aydin and Sönmez patients called 'Two siblings' in the Discussion but 'two cousins' in reference [20] title; Schulze 2003 (row 35) age 3 years but age of onset 4 years; Case 1 protein printed 'p.D135h' (Table 1) vs 'p.D135 h' (text); Case 3 printed 'x. 577c>T' / 'pQ193X' (non-standard, recorded as printed); Case 3 speech delay at age 2 years (text) vs age of onset 4 (Table 1); Case 4 Table 1 gives only 'c.406C >T' (zygosity from text). Reference [40] (Mudd 2001, row 39) title concerns glycine N-methyltransferase deficiency but Table 2 lists it as a GAMT case; extracted as listed. Possible duplicate literature patients across rows (e.g. Mercimek 2012 [29] row 16 vs rows 32-33; Sijens [26] rows 10 and 23; Stöckler [44]/[45] rows 44-45) were not merged. Table 1 age columns are in years (header 'Age (years)', 'Age of onset (years)'). Case 2's cousin with epilepsy and Case 1's two healthy siblings were not given rows (not tested, no GAMT-related status). cohort_size_as_stated = 45 literature cases; n_patients_reported left null because no single total (45 + 4) is stated. Case 2 'symmetric' power/tone/reflexes not used as normal.
